Introduction

Nevada licenses Agencies to Provide Personal Care Services in the Home to deliver non-medical care. The NV Department of Health & Human Services — Division of Public & Behavioral Health, HCQC oversees licensing.

Table of Contents

  • Understand Nevada’s Regulations
  • Choose the Type and Size of Agency
  • Business Structure and Licensing
  • Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan
  • Establish Operations Infrastructure
  • Hire and Train Qualified Staff
  • Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans
  • Marketing and Community Outreach
  • Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections
  • Frequently Asked Questions

1. Understand Nevada’s Regulations

DPBH/HCQC licenses personal care agencies under Nevada Revised Statutes. Requirements include licensing, background checks, training, and quality standards.

2. Choose the Type and Size of Agency

Services include personal care, homemaker, companion, and respite services.

3. Business Structure and Licensing

Register with the NV Secretary of State, apply for agency license, secure insurance, and obtain a state business license.

4. Develop a Comprehensive Business Plan

Nevada benchmarks: Private pay rates $22-$32/hour, Medicaid rates $16-$22/hour, break-even 12-18 months. Las Vegas and Reno are primary markets.

5. Establish Operations Infrastructure

Set up office, scheduling software, and documentation systems.

6. Hire and Train Qualified Staff

Nevada requires background checks and training for all personal care workers.

7. Policies, Procedures, and Care Plans

Develop policies meeting HCQC requirements.

8. Marketing and Community Outreach

Focus on Las Vegas, Reno, and Henderson metro areas. Build relationships with healthcare providers and senior communities.

9. Maintain Compliance and Prepare for Inspections

Maintain licensing, training records, and quality programs.

10. Frequently Asked Questions

How long does licensing take? Typically 60-90 days for complete applications.
